properties.decision:
PROPOSED FOR ANTHONY'S WORD, NOTHING DONE. From fact:the-served-tools-sorted-by-their-counts-109-used-5-cued-unfollowed-40-never-reached-6-steps-39-close-2026-10-30.
(1) FOLD CANDIDATES, a twin carries the job (class E, by counts on flo2.io and the two trials): set_artifact_checksum (43 calls) into set_artifact_checksums (391; already the bulk form of the same accept, mutual top-5 in the corpus); acknowledge_gap (13) into acknowledge_gaps (24); dimension_drift and dimension_drifts (0 and 0) into one; propagate_change (32) into propagate_from (406) taking a change id as its seed; verifies (49) into add_verification (541), which already takes `verifies`; graph_report (23) and graph_report_markdown (33) as one tool with a format. Each fold keeps the old name as a refusing stub for one release naming the new call.
(2) NOT FOLD, BUT RENAME OR REWORD: manual_work_ledger (2) vs report_manual_work (16), a read and a write told apart by word order; add_epoch vs plan_epoch (85 each); scan_nodes vs search_design (both heavily used, different jobs).
(3) THE 40 NEVER REACHED (class C): before any is retired, each gets a path an agent meets at the moment it would need it (a skill step or a cue naming it), and is re-counted. 7 of the 40 are not served through flo2.io's hub, and record_the_build is younger than the sample; those 8 are not candidates at all. Retirement candidates only after that, and only those still at zero: the reports evidence_report, forecast_readiness, frontier, ility_report, granularity_report, consumption_report, surprising_connections, readiness_report/gate_on.
BEFORE ANY OF IT: dec:a-tool-is-never-deleted-without-usage-evidence-across-projects-and-never-without-a-refusing-stub-first holds — evidence from more than one person's projects (today about 94% of calls are Anthony's agents), the 90-day re-run of the flo2.io baseline (about 2026-12-23), and a deprecating release with the stub.
properties.name: OPEN — which served tools are candidates to fold into a twin or retire, from the 2026-10-30 counts, and what must happen before any of them goes (nothing removed now)
properties.rationale: The counts tell the classes apart for the first time (BL-155's "unused or unreachable"): a cue followed or not says whether a tool was wanted where it was offered, and never cued plus never called says nobody met it. They do not yet carry the weight of a removal: two made-up projects in agent trials and one month of flo2.io dominated by one person. So this records the candidates and the bar, and decides nothing. Counter-arguments kept: a fold removes a name some MCP user's prompt or script may call (reflow2 MCP stays as-is; removal needs a deprecating release); the bulk forms answer an item-numbered refusal a singular never needed, so a fold must keep it; a report never called may be unreachable rather than unwanted, which (3) tests before it judges.
